{"lineage":"original","name":"A project can tell work that serves its own machinery apart from work that reaches its consumers, so "did we close a user-facing need with an internal fix?" is answerable from the graph","priority":"medium","provenance":"authored","statement":"A deliverable must be able to record WHO IT IS FOR — a consumer of the product, or the project's own machinery — and the design must then be able to answer, without asking a person: is there a need here that nothing consumer-facing delivers?

DELIBERATELY DISTINCT FROM `rule:reflow2-is-built-for-other-projects-not-for-itself` and from `rule:fixes-are-judged-by-the-third-party`, and the split is the point. Those RULES are how the people building reflow2 work; they bind this project and can never bind anyone else's. This REQUIREMENT is the product carrying the same philosophy, so every project using reflow2 inherits the question. That is the identical shape as `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, which exists because Anthony asked on 2026-08-17 for his building philosophy to be "built into the design of reflow2" rather than merely stated at its developers. A rule states it; a requirement makes it something reflow2 DOES.

ALSO DISTINCT FROM `req:a-fix-says-whether-it-corrected-the-cause`, which was surfaced as near: that one asks whether a repair reached the CAUSE or worked around it. This one asks who the work was FOR. A root-cause fix can still land entirely in internal machinery, and a workaround can ship straight to a consumer; the two axes are independent and both are currently unrecorded.

⭐ THE DISTINCTION IS UNIVERSAL, NOT REFLOW2'S. Every project that ships anything has internal machinery and a delivered product, and confuses them under pressure: a team's own scripts against what the beamline actually does, CI configuration against the library, a build tool against the API. The failure it enables is the same everywhere and it LOOKS LIKE COMPLETION — find a hole, patch it in the internal half, mark the need met, and leave every consumer with the hole. The repo goes green and nothing is true of anybody else.

⚠️ NEVER INFERRED FROM A PATH. A first sketch of this proposed classifying deliverables by directory — `.github/` internal, `crates/` shipped — which encodes ONE project's layout and is exactly the failure it exists to prevent. The audience is DECLARED by the project or it is unknown, and unknown is a true answer.

⚠️ AND NEVER A JUDGEMENT. Internal work is legitimate and necessary; a release procedure, a coordination board and an export discipline are real work that reaches no consumer. The requirement is that the difference be VISIBLE, never that internal work be discouraged (`dec:report-dont-judge`).

🛑 THE DETECTOR MUST SAY WHEN IT HAD NOTHING TO RUN ON. If no deliverable in a project has declared an audience, the reading is "I cannot judge this", NOT zero findings. A detector reporting zero because its population was empty reads exactly like one that ran clean — `loop_status` already refuses an unknown contributor_id for this reason, and this is the same trap one level over.

HONEST LIMIT, the same class as `provenance` and the drift dispositions: this records what the author SAYS a deliverable is for. It cannot detect an internal tool declared consumer-facing. Worth having because the alternative is no signal at all; worth never overselling.","status":"proposed"}
